title: Meeting Marian in the Ardennes
summary: On transfer to Special Service he first hears Marian play Honeysuckle Rose and is won over by her ballads.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Since we've mentioned (Achen?) and your marrying Marian (LAUGHTER) I think that it's probably as good a place as any to sort of talk about that. How you met her and....

Well, what happened was, we were patrolling around (Saints Vith? with) that's where the break through came in the Battle of the Bulge by the way. We were patrolling there in the Arden Forest in November. It was October or November and I

got a call one morning after I came off this patrol. I just came off the patrol and the colonel wanted to see me. I had put in before that that I wanted to go into Special Service and play the cornet again.

So the colonel called me in and says, Mc, he says, I got a call and I'm supposed to bring you over to Group Headquarters, 115th Group Headquarters for AAA automatic weapons. And we had those four 50-calibers mounted on the half tracks. And he says..oh, I had gotten busted again in Paris! (LAUGHTER). That's what happened. I had gotten busted again in Paris. Drinking too much of that brandy and you know, and cognac, cognac and champagne.

So I got busted there in Paris and I was a private again. But he says you don't have to go. He says, it's up to you if you want to go and play with the band there in Special Service or I'll make you a sergeant again. (LAUGHTER). I said, no sir. I don't want to be anything anymore colonel. I just want to blow that horn again. (LAUGHTER). I'll be very happy to blow that horn.
He said, well frankly I don't blame you. He says, if it were me I think I would do the same thing.

He said, Okay, get your gear together. So I went over to the V Corps Headquarters. The colonel took me over there and they were all, they were all bivouacked out in the Ardennes Forest and reported in. And I was mean at that time you know. Man, I was mean.
You were a gang boy again huh?

That's true. That's soldiering and you can have it. So they all asked me to, would I get the horn out and play, we were going to have a jam session. So I said, yes. I said, get me a bottle of scotch first and then I'll play. So they got a bottle of scotch, I went over all these musicians in the band there. And there's a piano and there's a girl sitting at the piano and I thought, oh no, a girl? And she spoke English. (LAUGHTER).

With a British accent. I thought, this is not it you know. And sure enough, what did Marian? (it was?) Honeysuckle Rose and she wanted to play it. And sure enough she started off playing and she was real excited you know. So she started playing and she was rushing like mad you know. I thought, oh no, this is not it.
But she did play it pretty good for a girl I thought, you know. (LAUGHTER). And after we had played

a few jazz numbers I said, do me a favor, play a ballad, play something pretty. Because I could hear her harmony, her left hand, and she was playing some good stuff there. And I knew my harmonies. And it was different you know. And her inversions, her piano, her bass. Very interesting harmonically. And good.
So she played these ballads for me and when she played the ballad she knocked me out. She was a musician you know.
Do you remember what some of the ballads were?
Can't remember that, well go ahead.
